etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Onomatopoeia. Compare bungle, jumble, and fumble.
senses: (intransitive) To act or move in an awkward or confused manner (often clumsily, incompetently, or carelessly). [from 1530s]
(originally Scotland and Northern England, transitive) To carry out (a task) clumsily, incompetently, or with many careless mistakes; to bungle, to botch. [from ca. 1719?]

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (intransitive) To boom, as a Eurasian bittern. [from ca. 1405]
(intransitive, of an insect) To buzz or bum. [from 1689]
